free_tier.stated: Los Angeles KVM: the cheapest paid plan is LAX.VPS.INTL.2C1G20G at USD 3.99 a month for 2 CPU vCores, 1GB RAM, 20GB SSD storage, 1TB monthly transfer, a 1Gbps port and 1 IPv4 plus 2 IPv6, with instant delivery and automatic provisioning. The order page also lists LAX.VPS.INTL.2C2G40G at USD 7.99 (2 CPU, 2GB, 40GB, 2TB), LAX.VPS.INTL.2C4G80G at USD 15.99 (2 CPU, 4GB, 80GB, 3TB), LAX.VPS.INTL.4C8G160G at USD 29.99 (4 CPU, 8GB, 160GB, 4TB), and the unmetered LAX.VPS.INTL.UM.2C4G40G at USD 39.00 (2 CPU, 4GB, 40GB, Unmetered transfer, 200Mbps port), all with 1 IPv4 plus 2 IPv6.

chaining: USD 3.99 is below the usual floor for a 2 vCPU machine with a dedicated IPv4, and it composes with free egress via a CDN in front, which removes the 1 TB cap from the serving path.

limits.value: The 1 TB monthly transfer at 1 Gbps is the binding term: sustained full-port traffic would exhaust it in about 2.2 hours, so the shape is a service box rather than a transfer engine. The China-optimised variant of the same 2 vCPU / 1 GiB shape costs USD 7.99, double.
